0.0.n: A playful, stretched-out greeting borrowed from Italian.

0.2.n: Part of the name みぽち; the supplied word split and reading are misleading.

0.3.n: This chunk contains the final ち of みぽち plus casual だ; it is not a verb.

0.4.n: Sentence-ending よ adds friendly emphasis, and the long vowel makes the introduction playful.

0.6.n: Used to launch the next part of the introduction, rather than answer a question.

0.8.n: やってまいりました is a polite, humble version of やってきました, used here as a show-opening announcement.

0.10.n: This begins the channel name みぽちゅーぶ, based on the speaker’s name.

0.11.n: This ち belongs to the channel name みぽちゅーぶ, not a separate word.

0.12.n: This completes the channel name; ちゅーぶ playfully echoes the English word tube.

1.0.n: An adjective can stand alone as an exclamation without adding a word for it or is.

1.2.n: Repeating the adjective emphasizes how strongly she feels the chill.

1.3.n: This further repetition makes the complaint sound spontaneous and emphatic.

1.5.n: Sets the time for the comment without needing a particle.

1.6.n: A very casual intensifier placed before the adjective.

1.7.n: The plain adjective connects directly to explanatory んだ.

1.8.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone before だ.

1.9.n: Completes explanatory んだ; it does not attach directly to 寒い on its own.

1.10.n: Links the complaint about the weather to her plan despite it.

1.12.n: Sets the time again, this time for the filming plan.

1.13.n: Marks today as another occasion when she is going out filming.

1.14.n: Points to what she is about to do next.

1.15.n: A place name for a district in Tokyo, specifying the filming location.

1.16.n: Short for ロケーション, commonly used for filming outside a studio.

1.17.n: Marks ロケ as the purpose of going, rather than directly marking Shibuya as the destination.

1.18.n: 行く becomes 行きたい to express a wish; with と思います, it gently announces a plan.

1.19.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

1.20.n: The polite form of 思う; after たい, it softens the announcement of an intention.

2.0.n: A casual connector used to move on to today’s topic.

2.2.n: Sets the time for the interviews.

2.3.n: Suggests she is doing interviews today as on previous occasions.

2.4.n: Adds a friendly conversational pause that draws the listener in.

2.6.n: 聞く in its て-form plus いく presents asking as an activity unfolding from now onward.

2.7.n: Turns 聞いていく into a noun-like phrase: what she will be asking.

2.8.n: Marks 聞いていくの as the subject, though she later restarts the sentence with を聞いていきたい.

2.10.n: Part of 黒歴史, a set expression for an embarrassing past, not literally a color description here.

2.11.n: Together with 黒, forms 黒歴史: memories or phases someone would rather hide.

2.12.n: Joins the two topics she plans to ask about.

2.13.n: Combines with まで to form 今まで, covering someone’s life up to the present.

2.14.n: Marks the endpoint in 今まで, meaning the period ending now.

2.15.n: Sets 今まで as the range for comparing which mistake was the biggest.

2.16.n: Makes the following mistake the biggest one in the person’s experience.

2.17.n: Casual contraction of やらかしてしまった; the past form suggests a regrettable blunder.

2.18.n: Refers to the incident described by やらかしちゃった immediately before it.

2.19.n: Marks the embarrassing experiences as what she wants to ask about.

2.20.n: 聞いていく becomes 聞いていきたい, expressing her intention to ask people as the filming proceeds.

2.21.n: Links her stated wish to 思います.

2.22.n: Polite 思います softens たい into a friendly announcement of what she plans to do.

3.0.n: Drop the final い of 寒い and add すぎる to say the degree is excessive.

3.1.n: Contrasts the extreme cold with her determination to keep going.

3.2.n: Refers to the drink she is showing or holding.

3.3.n: Marks これ as what she will drink.

3.4.n: The て-form of 飲む links drinking to the following action.

3.5.n: The plain form expresses her resolve to push through the cold.

3.7.n: An energetic expression borrowed directly from English.

0.lit: Ciao, it’s Mipochi! Okay, here we have come: Mipochube.
0.tip: みぽち and みぽちゅーぶ are names, despite the misleading word splits.

1.lit: Cold! Cold, cold. Today, super cold, but today too, from now, I think I want to go for Shibuya filming.
1.tip: 行きたいと思います politely announces a plan rather than merely reporting a thought.

2.lit: And today too, what I’ll ask: embarrassing pasts and the biggest thing messed up so far, I want to ask.
2.tip: 黒歴史 means an embarrassing past someone would rather forget, not literal black history.

3.lit: It’s too cold, but I’ll drink this and do my best. Let’s go!
3.tip: 飲んで links two actions: drinking this, then pressing on.
